intro: Seoul rewards visitors with royal palaces, mountain trails, street food and endless nightlife. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metro: 9 numbered lines plus suburban lines; base fare ₩1,550 with card, ₩1,650 single ticket.
Buses have own lanes and beat traffic; use a T-money card for both bus and metro.
Taxis are metered and plentiful; Kakao T is the main ride-hailing app, Uber works too.
Climate Card gives 1-7 day unlimited passes from ₩5,000 to ₩20,000.
Driving is possible but traffic jams are common; parking is costly.
Subway stops late at night; night buses run on major routes.

gyeongbokgung.price_text: KRW 3,000 adults · free if you wear hanbok
gyeongbokgung.hours: Closed Tuesday · usually 09:00–18:00, shorter in winter — check on the day

bukchon.name: Bukchon Hanok Village

changdeokgung.name: Changdeokgung Palace and Huwon

ddp.name: Dongdaemun Design Plaza
ddp.price_text: Free to enter the building · exhibitions ticketed

gwanghwamun.name: Gwanghwamun Square
gwanghwamun.tip: Good starting point — the palace gate is right in front of you.

myeongdongcathedral.name: Myeongdong Cathedral

myeongdongcathedral.tip: Step inside quietly; the shopping street is right below.

jongmyo.name: Jongmyo Shrine

lottetower.name: Lotte World Tower

aquaplanet.name: Aqua Planet Ilsan
aquaplanet.price_text: Ticket price varies — check on the day

bongeunsa.name: Bongeunsa Temple
bongeunsa.tip: A quiet temple right across from the COEX mall — a good contrast stop.

bugaksan.name: Bugaksan
bugaksan.price_text: Free · ID required for the trail
bugaksan.hours: Trail hours limited — check on the day

coexaquarium.name: COEX Aquarium
coexaquarium.price_text: Ticket price varies — check on the day

changgyeonggung.name: Changgyeonggung Palace
changgyeonggung.tip: Quieter than its neighbours; walk here after Changdeokgung.

cheonggyecheon.name: Cheonggyecheon Stream
cheonggyecheon.tip: Walk the stream at night when the lights come on.

cheongwadae.name: Cheongwadae
cheongwadae.tip: Reserve a slot online before you go.

deoksugung.name: Deoksugung Palace
deoksugung.tip: Easy to reach from City Hall; the stone-wall path is lovely in autumn.

ewha.name: Ewha Womans University
ewha.tip: The sunken glass building and the shopping street nearby are the draw.

gangnamstatue.name: Gangnam Style Horse Dance Statue
gangnamstatue.tip: A quick photo stop outside COEX — don't plan more than a few minutes.

gwangjang.name: Gwangjang Market food stalls
gwangjang.price_text: Street food roughly KRW 5,000–15,000 per dish
gwangjang.hours: Stalls roughly 09:00–23:00 — check on the day
gwangjang.tip: Sit at a stall and try bindaetteok and mayak gimbap.

namsanwalk.name: Namsan Park walk
namsanwalk.tip: Walk up from Myeongdong instead of taking the cable car.

hanoktour.name: Hanbok rental and palace photo walk
hanoktour.price_text: Rental roughly KRW 15,000–30,000 for a few hours — check on the day

myeongdongfood.name: Myeongdong street food walk
myeongdongfood.tip: Bring small cash and eat where the locals queue.

hongdaenight.name: Hongdae bar and live-music night

gangnamwalk.name: Gangnam and COEX neighbourhood walk

p63building.name: 63 Building
p63building.price_text: Observation deck price varies — check on the day
p63building.tip: The riverside view at dusk is the reason to come.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Palaces, hanok lanes and the city's best museums.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Markets, BBQ and all-night street snacks.

styles.label: Shopping
styles.blurb: Myeongdong cosmetics, Dongdaemun and Gangnam malls.

stays.why: Walk to the shopping streets, Namsan and the subway hub at Myeongdong station. Easiest base for first-timers.
Next to Gyeongbokgung, Bukchon hanok lanes and Insadong. Quiet at night, central for sightseeing.
Modern hotels, big malls and nightlife. Good for business trips; longer rides to the old palaces.
Cheapest of the four, young and lively, close to the airport rail link. Noisy on weekend nights.

food.tip: Eat at Gwangjang Market: bindaetteok (mung-bean pancakes), mayak gimbap and knife-cut noodles. Expect roughly ₩5,000–12,000 a plate.
Korean BBQ is a group meal. Order pork belly or beef, wrap it in lettuce with garlic; expect ₩15,000–30,000 per person.
Street snacks in Myeongdong and Hongdae: tteokbokki, hotteok and fried chicken. Most items cost ₩3,000–8,000.
Cheap and filling: gimbap shops and university-area restaurants serve a full meal for about ₩6,000–10,000.
Many restaurants are open late. Look for 24-hour spots around markets and Hongdae; check on the day for closing times.

more_time.swap: Add a day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress or the DMZ tour; both need a full day, book ahead.
Swap one shopping afternoon for a Han River picnic and a bike rental at Yeouido.
Spend a morning in a jjimjilbang (Korean spa) or a palace hanbok rental instead of another museum.
